mike_customer: Hey, running into a repeatable issue where our mobile clients on CarrierX drop mid-stream after ~30s. No HTTP error, client shows ECONNRESET and we get only partial output (last token missing). Anyone seen carrier NAT timeouts cause this?
jess_support: ugh. can you repro with curl -N? also share request_id if you have one.
mike_customer: repro'd with curl. stream opens, we get data for ~29-31s then connection drops with zero-length last event. curl exit code 56. Here's reproduction command: `curl -N -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream\"`
mike_customer: request_id=rid_20231021_9f8c3e
jess_support: thx. quick thought: mobile carriers often have NAT timeouts ~30s. SSE needs either intermediate keep-alives or more frequent chunking to keep NAT state alive. can you paste server logs around that request_id?
mike_customer: pasted a snippet: ```[2024-11-02T14:21:07Z] rid_20231021_9f8c3e upstream write error: write tcp 10.12.4.5:443->100.101.102.103:54321: write: connection reset by peer```

jess_support: that matches client-side reset. two parallel asks: 1) try client-side heartbeat: send a 1-byte SSE comment `:keepalive\n\n` every 15s from the server 2) try curl with `--no-buffer` and also test from wifi vs carrier to confirm.
mike_customer: tried adding comment events from our proxy, still saw drop at ~31s when on CarrierX. on wifi it's stable.
sam_eng: pinging eng-runtime. @ria_eng_runtime can you weigh in? Could be proxy timeout (nginx/gcloud tcp idle) or intermediate CGNAT.
ria_eng_runtime: likely CGNAT + carrier idle. Quick checklist: - ensure upstream (our front proxy) sends TCP keepalive or SSE comment at <20s - if using nginx, increase `proxy_read_timeout` and `proxy_send_timeout` and `send_timeout` - for gcp/elb, there are idle timeouts to adjust. Also check if proxies buffer events until buffer flush threshold, causing no bytes over wire for 30s.

jess_support: good point about buffering. are you using chunked flush? many frameworks buffer until event size > x or on flush call. If buffered, NAT sees quiet and drops.
mike_customer: we're on our own k8s ingress (traefik) + app server (node). traefik has `forwarder` timeouts? we didn't tune keepalive.

sam_eng: temporary workaround from our side: enable periodic SSE comment from the Redwood edge for that customer route. That will keep NAT alive without app changes. Would need a safe opt-in though.

olivia_oncall: deploy-bot reports: `deploy queued for opt-in-edge-heartbeat (canary)`
deploy-bot: build 4521 started for service: edge-proxy, config: opt-in-heartbeat-ttl=15s
jess_support: @mike_customer if you want to try that, we can opt your project into edge-heartbeat; it'll send `:hb\n\n` every 15s from the edge when streaming. It's not enabled by default because it increases small writes.
mike_customer: please opt us in for a canary. that would help us confirm.

ria_eng_runtime: also sending blocking note: if application server buffers, edge heartbeat alone won't help. but useful diagnostic: enable our edge heartbeat and run curl -i to see if bytes arrive in steady intervals. `curl -N -i` should show intermittent `:hb` comment lines.
jess_support: repro step for your team: 1) opt-in edge-heartbeat 2) run `curl -N -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" -i \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?project=yourproj\"` 3) observe server bytes; note time between bytes and when connection closes.
mike_customer: will try. also attaching tcpdump and client logs after next run.

sam_eng: noted escalation to eng-runtime. @ria_eng_runtime please flag any edge perf concerns; we need to ensure heartbeat doesn't degrade throughput for bursty workloads.
ria_eng_runtime: will monitor. if we see high CPU from extra small writes we'll switch to adaptive heartbeat: only during first 60s of stream.

mike_customer: quick update: after opt-in, I see `:hb` every 15s. carrier still cut at 31s but curl now shows `:hb` at 15s and 30s, then connection still reset immediately after the 30s heartbeat arrives. tcpdump shows FIN from carrier side. so maybe carrier resets sessions at 31s regardless of traffic.
jess_support: that's useful — suggests carrier enforced maximum session window or middlebox with connection churn policy. two more options: 1) implement client reconnect/resume so partial outputs are stitched (we can help with resume tokens) 2) switch to websocket where carrier may treat differently (not guaranteed).
mike_customer: reconnect/resume sounds good. how to resume without duplicating tokens?
sam_eng: we have a resume token pattern: server emits `event: resume_token\ndata: <token>\n\n` periodically. client reconnects with `?resume_token=` and server will continue from offset. will open an RFC doc link.
jess_support: for immediate mitigation we can also increase server-side chunking frequency: flush every 5-10 tokens instead of waiting for sentence end. that increases bytes on wire and helps NATs.

mike_customer: ok we're going to implement resume_token and smaller flushes on our side. thanks. will report back after testing on CarrierX.
jess_support: thanks — ping us with request_id and tcpdump if it persists and we'll escalate to network partners. :thumbsup:

mike_customer: thanks everyone. filing follow-up ticket with logs.

olivia_oncall: marking this thread for postmortem if it affects >3 customers.

jess_support: closing loop: action items captured: [opt-in edge-heartbeat canary], [customer implement resume_token], [eng-runtime monitor edge perf], [support to collect tcpdump + request_id if persists].

mike_customer: added ticket #SUP-9923. last_message_ts=2101234599
